speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To begin my examination of this newborn with a generalized rash, please tell me how many days old the infant is and when you first noticed the skin changes.

speaker: Patient
text: 4-day-old newborn. The newborn was born at term with no complications. The mother had no prenatal care and has a history of gonorrhea treated 4 years ago. The newborn presents with a generalized rash that has been present for 1 day.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details. Since the rash appeared 3 days after birth, please describe the specific appearance of the lesions and if they are blanching or purpuric. Also, are there any signs of systemic infection such as fever, poor feeding, or lethargy?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Generalized erythematous maculopapular rash and pustules. I also have Rash with an erythematous base, Rash over the trunk and extremities, Sparing of the palms and soles.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Neonatal Gonococcal Infection (Disseminated).

The description of a pustular rash with an erythematous base and sparing of the palms and soles in a 4-day-old infant is classic for disseminated gonococcal infection. I will order a Gram stain and culture of the pustules and blood cultures to confirm the diagnosis. REQUEST TEST: Blood_Culture, Skin_Pus_Gram_Stain, Skin_Pus_Culture.
